hardware: Apple M3, 10-core GPU, 16 GB RAM; eight CPU threads
changes: Exact IEEE FP32 comparison uses integer bit ordering instead of conversion to software binary64. NaNs remain unordered, signed zeros equal, and subnormal/infinite ordering is preserved. Split gain arithmetic and tie rules are unchanged.

Packed input initializes only alignment padding before appending its owned payload. This removes zero writes immediately overwritten by copying, preserving input ownership, offsets, counters and command boundaries.
The existing training profiler adds seven-class Covertype, synthetic categorical data, optional missing values and post-validation current RSS. Large profiles remain outside tests.

expected_skips: Linux-only ELF loader check on macOS
No-accessible-Metal negative check on a host with a GPU
full_regression.scope: Full standard suite on clean 28908e1 before this optimization. CPU-only/federated optional builds and actual NVIDIA execution are separate gates.

candidate_correctness.command: bash scripts/test.sh --native metal_input_api metal_columnar_api metal_cuda_split metal_cuda_multi_split metal_split_finalize metal_feature_split_api metal_split_categories --python tests/test_metal_input.py tests/test_metal_columnar.py tests/test_metal_prediction.py tests/test_metal_training.py tests/test_metal_workflows.py tests/test_metal_cuda_splits.py tests/test_metal_cuda_multi_splits.py tests/test_metal_split_categories.py --log-dir results/regression-tuning-20261106T195227Z/candidate-check
candidate_correctness.scope: Focused acceptance on the final candidate; full standard suite above predates these two optimizations. Same-model CPU prediction is checked exactly by every MPS profiling worker.

comparator_microbenchmark.assessment: Strong categorical benefit in every pair; numeric and one-hot gains are mixed. Numeric missing 1024-task case regresses about9.1% median. End-to-end controls needed; categorical-only specialization is an alternative if regression persists.

rejected_or_deferred_experiments.histogram_direct_store: Rejected: all 1024 outputs match CPU exactly, but 56 of 64 measured cases are slower. Production histogram kernels are unchanged.
rejected_or_deferred_experiments.workspace_retention: Deferred after the current profile: 1.1% of main-thread samples are in split allocations, with a potentially longer high-water allocation lifetime. The prototype passed five native groups and 298 Python tests, including three baseline-validated reconfiguration cases. No timing gain is claimed; it was fully reverted before the final candidate.
rejected_or_deferred_experiments.candidate: Exact FP32 bit comparison and redundant input-zero-fill removal pass seven native groups and 427 Python tests. Targeted categorical training improves 1.80x; missing-value training is effectively flat, and wide timing is mixed/slower amid paging variation. The broader workload results are recorded separately.

histogram_prototype.decision: Do not promote the direct-store shader change. Leave production and clearing unchanged.
histogram_prototype.change: Only tiled histogram merges for nodes with exactly one row block store the low/high words directly; other nodes retain atomic addition.
histogram_prototype.timing_scope: Command GPU elapsed time includes the unchanged histogram clear and kernel, with one warmup and seven shuffled paired repeats per variant and geometry.

coverage: 2-bit and 8-bit compressed indices split across head/tail storage

assessment.reason: The intended wide single-block workloads regress consistently. Direct stores write zero words that add_i64 can skip; this is a plausible explanation, not an isolated hardware diagnosis. Small positive differences are confined to narrow microcases and include unchanged multi-block paths.

limits: Fresh processes, warmed runtime, depth 6, max_bin 256, eight CPU threads. Training includes quantization and evaluation each round. Loading/generation, DMatrix creation and final prediction are excluded and reported separately.

Three paired CPU/candidate repeats per workload. Targeted workloads also have three baseline MPS repeats; long workloads have only one baseline reference, which supports correctness but not a robust before/after timing claim.

No local builds/tests/other benchmarks from this task ran during timings. Other applications were not controlled; system-wide paging substantially affected the wide workload. Retain every repeat and do not mix ratios with earlier sessions.
GPU command boundaries are unchanged between 28908e1 and this candidate. Counter families may overlap and are not pure kernel times; do not sum them or infer CPU time by subtraction.

Current memory.after RSS is sampled after prediction, model saving and CPU validation, not immediately after training. It does not represent the complete Metal physical footprint. Swap is system-wide.
Exact MPS before/after outputs do not imply independent CPU/MPS training equivalence. No actual NVIDIA comparison or additional Apple hardware was used.
